quotes.text: On 2026-11-16 a run sat 9 hours because a fixer never ran `rhiza session done` and its conductor's spawn waited on it. ... The daemon should detect and recover (nudge, then retry or fail the step with a reason), for every workflow's agent steps.

The daemon's stall detection needs the same distinction (idle with a live background job vs idle with nothing running), read portably (ps on Linux and macOS), with a longer bound for the background case, and the runaway check reads the same process tree.

fields.summary: The conductor of run 01M7QBNRXR planned change set 01M7NVMG (m40-stalls) with no owner present, from the milestone-40 brief (hands-off-milestone-interview.md, point 2 and point 9) and the orchestrator's planner notes for m40-stalls. Research found the watchdog's stalled-step pass (watchdogStalled) and the session nudge (daemonNudgeStalled) read a step's sessions through stepSessions in internal/api/run.go, which covers the step's own session, leaves, checks and change-set fixers but never the children of rhiza run spawn (run.State.Spawns), so a conductor's idle child is never nudged and the conductor's own long-running spawn command is what goes silent. The planner notes' idle-with-a-background-job distinction needs the agent's process tree, which the runaway change set (m40-runaway) reads, so it is drafted apart. No owner words: autonomous run.
fields.title: Stall change set plan, autonomous conduct run 01M7QBNRXR
